top_choice_rationale: P001 (Autor, Hanson, Dorn) best meets the common criteria of originality, testing and attributable credit. The China-shock and local-labour-market papers pose a first-order question about who bears the cost of trade and technology change. They use transparent designs and have been replicated, re-analysed and contested for roughly a decade. That contest concerns the size and persistence of the effects, not whether adjustment is slow and costly. Autor, Dorn and Hanson jointly authored the central papers, so three names are accurate if the citation is limited to the empirical evidence and does not claim the task-model theory, whose originators lie outside the credited set. P002 (Melitz, Helpman) is a strong and cleanly credited second choice, with a long confirmation record on firm microdata. It is exposed to the Bernard-Jensen and Eaton-Kortum attribution questions and to functional-form dependence in its welfare results. I regard the gap between the two as a close weighting judgement. An award is preferable to no award, so P000 is last.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my frequent co-authors (Bayer, Anwar, Lindquist, Holmlund, Lochner, Bindler) are not credited names on P001 or P002, and my labour-economics and crime research is adjacent in subject only, which I treat as expertise and not as a tie.
